paper.title: Learning Neural Contextual Bandits Through Perturbed Rewards

settings.name_in_paper: Contextual bandit with finite K arms and neural (NTK) reward mapping
unmapped: Each of the K arms has a fixed d-dimensional context vector x_i (unit norm, symmetric halves); unknown reward function h with 0<=h<=1 approximated by a ReLU network of width m and depth L
NTK matrix H on the context set satisfies H >= lambda_0 I
Reward norm bound S upper-bounds sqrt(2 h^T H^{-1} h) (RKHS norm of h in the NTK space)
Perturbation scale is set using lambda_K(A_K), the K-th largest eigenvalue of the covariance matrix after the initial K pulls
settings.definition_quote: We study the problem of contextual bandit with finite $K$ arms, where each arm is associated with a $d$-dimensional context vector: $\xb_i \in \RR^d$ for $i \in [K]$. At each round $t \in [T]$, the agent needs to select one of the arms, denoted as $a_t$, and receives its reward $r_{a_t, t}$, which is generated as $r_{a_t, t} = h(\xb_{a_t}) + \eta_{t}$. In particular, $h(\xb)$ represents the unknown underlying reward mapping function satisfying $0 \leq h(\xb) \leq 1$ for any $\xb$, and $\eta_{t}$ is an $R$-sub-Gaussian random variable

bound.expression: 44*E*sqrt(pi)*(1 + sqrt((4*log(T) + 2*log(K))/(1 - lam/lam_KA)))*(sigma*sqrt(d_eff*log(1 + T*K/lam) + 2 - 2*log(delta)) + sqrt(lam)*S)*sqrt(2*d_eff*T*log(1 + T*K/lam) + 2) + 7 + K
bound.expression_latex: R_T \leq \Gamma \Big(R\sqrt{\tilde{d}\log(1 + TK/\lambda) +2 - 2\log \delta} + \sqrt{\lambda}S\Big)\cdot\sqrt{2\tilde dT\log(1+TK/\lambda) +2} + 7 + K, \Gamma = 44\eb \sqrt{\pi} (1 + \sqrt{(4\log T + 2\log K) / (1 - \lambda \lambda_K^{-1}(\Ab_K))})

symbols.lam_KA: K-th largest eigenvalue of the covariance matrix A_K built after the initial K pulls

conditions: Assumption 9: NTK matrix H >= lambda_0 I, ||x_i||_2 = 1, [x_i]_j = [x_i]_{j+d/2}
d_eff is the effective dimension of the NTK matrix: log det(I + T H/lambda)/log(1+TK/lambda)
tuning: eta = C_1 (m T L + m lambda)^{-1}
number of GD steps J chosen as in the proof

source.label: thm:regret
source.quote: Let $\tilde d$ be the effective dimension of the NTK kernel matrix $\Hb$. There exist positive constants $C_1$ and $C_r$, such that for any $\delta \in(0, 1)$, when network structure and the step size for model update satisfy $m \geq \text{poly}(T, L, K, \lambda^{-1}, S^{-1}, \log(1/\delta))$, $\eta = C_1( mTL +  m \lambda)^{-1}$ and $\lambda \geq \max\{1, S^{-2}\}$, with probability at least $1-\delta$, the cumulative regret of \model{} satisfies R_T \leq \Gamma (R\sqrt{\tilde{d}\log(1 + TK/\lambda) +2 - 2\log \delta} + \sqrt{\lambda}S)\cdot\sqrt{2\tilde dT\log(1+TK/\lambda) +2} + 7 + K

results.notes: R_T is defined as E[sum (r_{a*} - r_{a_t})], i.e. through expected rewards, so it is recorded as pseudo-regret; the 1-delta probability is over network initialization and the confidence events. The paper's R (sub-Gaussian parameter) is mapped to sigma. The paper's perturbation std (also called sigma/nu) is an algorithm parameter and is described in tuning. The abstract summarises this bound as O~(d_eff sqrt(T)). Setting choices are judgement calls: the contexts are a fixed set of K vectors in the theory, so context=none; NTK reward modelling is mapped to kernel_rkhs with reward_model neural_ntk.
